system:
You extract quantitative facts about one clinical trial programme from one document.

Rules:
- Extract only facts stated in THIS document. Never use outside knowledge.
- Every fact needs "quote": an exact, verbatim span copied from the document (8-300 characters) that contains the number. Quotes are machine-checked; paraphrases are discarded.
- Placebo-adjusted values are preferred. If a value is within-arm (not placebo-adjusted), set attrs.placebo_adjusted=false.
- Units: keep the unit the document uses; put it in "unit".
- Other trials of the same investigational drug (phase 2, dose-finding, other populations, combination arms) belong
  to the programme: extract their facts too, and put the trial's name in attrs.trial when the document gives it.
- Return {"facts": []} only if the document reports no results for the investigational drug.

Allowed keys:
  n_randomized, median_followup, primary_endpoint, inclusion_threshold, planned_events, assumed_rrr, power,
  alpha, stopped_early, events_treatment, events_control, events_total, hr, ci_low, ci_high, p_value,
  biomarker_change, baseline_level, sbp_change, safety_signal, readout_statement

For biomarker_change and baseline_level, attrs must include: biomarker (one of LDL-C, non-HDL-C, apoB, HDL-C,
Lp(a), triglycerides, hsCRP, IL-6, Lp-PLA2 activity, sPLA2-IIA, SBP, other), phase (phase2 or phase3),
timepoint, method (assay or "not stated"), placebo_adjusted (true/false), dose (if stated).
For biomarker_change give "value" as the change (negative = reduction) and state in attrs.kind whether it is
"percent" or "absolute".

Return JSON only:
{"facts": [{"key": "...", "value": <number or string>, "unit": "...", "attrs": {...}, "quote": "..."}]}
prompt:
Trial: ACCORD NCT00000620 - Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD)
Investigational drug: fenofibrate
Document: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00000620 ACCORD (registry, published 1999-10-28, source ctgov:NCT00000620@2010-03-14)

--- DOCUMENT TEXT ---
ClinicalTrials.gov record NCT00000620 (ACCORD)
Title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD)
Official title: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes (ACCORD)
Sponsor: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI)
Phase: PHASE3
Conditions: Atherosclerosis; Cardiovascular Diseases; Hypercholesterolemia; Hypertension; Diabetes Mellitus, Type 2; Diabetes Mellitus; Coronary Disease
Interventions: Anti-hyperglycemic Agents (DRUG); Anti-hypertensive Agents (DRUG); Blinded fenofibrate or placebo plus simvastatin (DRUG)
Start date: 1999-09
Enrollment: 10251 (ACTUAL)
Primary outcome(s): First Occurrence of a Major Cardiovascular Event (MCE); Specifically Nonfatal Heart Attack, Nonfatal Stroke, or Cardiovascular Death (Measured Throughout the Study) in the Glycemia Trial. [4.9 years] | First Occurrence of Major Cardiovascular Event (MCE) in the Blood Pressure Trial. [4.7 years] | First Occurrence of Major Cardiovascular Event (MCE) in the Lipid Trial. [4.7 years]
Eligibility criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus, as determined by the new American Diabetes Association guidelines, which include a fasting plasma glucose level greater than 126 mg/dl (7.0 mmol/l), or a 2-hour postload value in the oral glucose tolerance test of greater than 200 mg/dl, with confirmation by a retest
* For participants aged 40 years or older, history of CVD (heart attack, stroke, history of coronary revascularization, history of peripheral or carotid revascularization, or demonstrated angina)
* For participants aged 55 years or older, a history of CVD is not required, but participant must be considered to be at high risk for experiencing a CVD event due to existing CVD, subclinical disease, or 2+ CVD risk factors
* HbA1c 7.5%-9% (if on more drugs) or 7.5%-11% (if on fewer drugs)
Brief summary: The purpose of this study is to prevent major cardiovascular events (heart attack, stroke, or cardiovascular death) in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus using intensive glycemic control, intensive blood pressure control, and multiple lipid management.
--- END ---

Extract the facts.
